en.headline: High Court rejects mainland families' challenge to university fee rules
en.dek: Judge Russell Coleman ruled the Education Bureau's two-year residency requirement for subsidised places from 2028 is not irrational.
body: The High Court on Friday dismissed a judicial review brought by 87 mainland Chinese families who arrived under talent visa schemes, challenging a government policy that requires their children to have lived in Hong Kong for at least two years before qualifying for subsidised university places from the 2028 academic year.

High Court Judge Russell Coleman found no irrationality in the Education Bureau's approach. The policy, announced in July 2025, introduces a transitional one-year residency rule for the 2027-28 academic year. Currently, dependant visa holders who arrived as minors are treated as local students and pay about HK$47,000 in annual tuition for government-funded programmes, while non-local students pay three times that amount.

Coleman said the policy had been well considered by the authorities and that it was not the court's role to determine government policy unless questions of legality arose. He noted that quashing the measure would likely result in the same decision being made again.

zh.headline: 高院駁回內地人才計劃家庭挑戰大學學費政策
zh.dek: 法官裁定教育局要求子女須居港至少兩年才可享資助學額的政策並非不合理，由2028年起生效。
body: 高等法院星期五駁回87個透過人才簽證計劃來港的內地家庭提出的司法覆核，挑戰政府政策要求其子女須在港居住至少兩年，方可由2028學年起享有資助大學學額。
高等法院法官高浩文裁定教育局的做法並無不合理之處。該政策於2025年7月公布，2027-28學年申請將設過渡性一年居港要求。現時以未成年身份獲批受養人簽證的學生被視為本地生，政府資助課程年學費約4.7萬元，而非本地生則須支付三倍學費。
法官表示政策已獲當局充分考慮，除非涉及合法性問題，否則法院不宜介入政府政策決定。他指出即使撤銷該措施，當局很大可能會再作出相同決定。
